# Range invalid, finalize segment [S1]

The claim states that the evidence supports the method of reducing line segments in a hand-drawn Transfer Function (TF) using a sliding window approach to reduce computational cost. Source [S1] explicitly describes this method: it uses an error tolerance window for every vertex to simplify the TF, handles hand-drawn TFs to reduce noise from tremors, and aims to improve rendering speed by reducing the number of line segments. The notes and passages confirm that increasing the window size reduces the number of segments (and thus computational cost) but degrades image quality, and that a pre-filtering step is used. All facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
